class_data.name: Martial Arts
class_data.notes:
Your training grants you mastery of unarmed combat and certain weapons. Your Monk weapons are Simple melee weapons and Martial melee weapons with the Light property.

While you are unarmored, not wielding a Shield, and wielding only Monk weapons (or no weapons), you gain the following benefits:
• Bonus Unarmed Strike. You can make one Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action.
• Martial Arts Die. You can use a d6 in place of the normal damage of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons; this die increases as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the class table.
• Dexterous Attacks. You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons. When you use your Unarmed Strike to Grapple or Shove, you can use Dexterity instead of Strength to determine the save DC.

class_data.name: Unarmored Defense
class_data.notes: While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.

class_data.name: Monk’s Focus
class_data.notes:
You gain a pool of Focus Points that fuels certain Monk features. The number of points is shown in the class table. You regain all expended Focus Points when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Some features that use Focus Points require a saving throw; the DC equals 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.

You start knowing the following options:
• Flurry of Blows. You can spend 1 Focus Point to make two Unarmed Strikes as a Bonus Action.
• Patient Defense. You can take the Disengage action as a Bonus Action. Alternatively, you can spend 1 Focus Point to take both the Disengage and Dodge actions as a Bonus Action.
• Step of the Wind. You can take the Dash action as a Bonus Action. Alternatively, you can spend 1 Focus Point to take both the Disengage and Dash actions as a Bonus Action, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

class_data.name: Unarmored Movement
class_data.notes: While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your Speed increases by 10 feet. This bonus increases at higher Monk levels, as shown in the class table.

class_data.name: Uncanny Metabolism
class_data.notes:
When you roll Initiative, you can instantly regain all expended Focus Points. When you do, roll your Martial Arts die and regain Hit Points equal to your Monk level + the number rolled.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

class_data.name: Deflect Attacks
class_data.notes:
When a creature hits you with an attack that deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can use a Reaction to reduce the total damage to you by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can spend 1 Focus Point to redirect the attack. Choose a creature you can see: within 5 feet of you if the original attack was melee, or within 60 feet and not behind Total Cover if it was ranged. That creature must make a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die + your Dexterity modifier, of the same type as the original attack.

class_data.name: Subclass Feature
class_data.notes: You choose a Monk subclass and gain its level 3 feature. You gain additional subclass features at higher Monk levels.

class_data.name: Ability Score Improvement
class_data.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at levels 8, 12, and 16.

class_data.name: Slow Fall
class_data.notes: When you fall, you can use a Reaction to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

class_data.name: Extra Attack
class_data.notes: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

class_data.name: Stunning Strike
class_data.notes:
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can spend 1 Focus Point to attempt to stun it. The target must make a Constitution saving throw.
On a failed save, it is Stunned until the start of your next turn.
On a successful save, its Speed is halved until the start of your next turn, and the next attack roll made against it before then has Advantage.

subclass_data.name: Shadow Arts
subclass_data.notes:
You draw upon the power of the Shadowfell, gaining the following benefits:

Darkness. Expend 1 Focus Point to cast the Darkness spell without components. You can see within its area. At the start of each of your turns, you may move the area of Darkness to a space within 60 feet.

Darkvision. You gain Darkvision out to 60 feet; if you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet.

Shadowy Figments. You know the Minor Illusion spell. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

class_data.name: Fighting Style
class_data.notes:
You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Defense is recommended.
Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

class_data.name: Second Wind
class_data.notes:
As a Bonus Action, you can regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 + your Fighter level.
You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
You gain additional uses at higher levels as shown in the class table.

class_data.name: Weapon Mastery
class_data.notes:
You can use the mastery properties of three Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Each Long Rest, you may change one weapon choice.
You gain access to additional mastery options as you gain Fighter levels.

class_data.name: Action Surge
class_data.notes:
On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action.
Once used, you must finish a Short or Long Rest before using it again.
At level 17, you can use this feature twice between rests but only once per turn.

class_data.name: Tactical Mind
class_data.notes: When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of Second Wind to add 1d10 to the result instead of regaining Hit Points. If the check still fails, the use of Second Wind is not expended.

class_data.name: Subclass Feature
class_data.notes: You gain a Fighter subclass of your choice and its level 3 feature.

subclass_data.name: Spellcasting
subclass_data.notes:
You have learned to cast spells using the rules of spellcasting from chapter 7.

Cantrips. You know two Wizard cantrips of your choice. Recommended: Ray of Frost and Shocking Grasp. You can replace one cantrip whenever you gain a Fighter level. At level 10, you learn an additional Wizard cantrip.

Spell Slots. You use the Eldritch Knight Spellcasting table to determine how many spell slots you have. All expended slots return when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells. You prepare three level 1 Wizard spells at level 3. Recommended: Burning Hands, Jump, Shield. Your number of prepared spells increases as shown in the subclass table. Prepared spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. When you gain a Fighter level, you can replace one prepared spell.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

subclass_data.name: War Bond
subclass_data.notes:
You perform a 1-hour ritual (Short Rest allowed) to create a magical bond with a weapon. The bond fails if another Fighter is bonded to the weapon or if the weapon is attuned by another creature.

Once bonded, you cannot be disarmed of the weapon unless Incapacitated. If the weapon is on the same plane, you can summon it as a Bonus Action, teleporting it immediately to your hand.

You can bond with up to two weapons but can summon only one at a time. Bonding a third weapon breaks an existing bond of your choice.

effects.name: Draconic Ancestry
effects.notes: Your lineage stems from a dragon progenitor. Choose the kind of dragon from the Draconic Ancestors table. Your choice affects your Breath Weapon and Damage Resistance traits as well as your appearance.

effects.name: Breath Weapon
effects.notes: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with an exhalation of magical energy in either a 15-foot Cone or a 30-foot Line that is 5 feet wide (choose the shape each time). Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, a creature takes 1d10 damage of the type determined by your Draconic Ancestry trait. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. This damage increases by 1d10 when you reach character levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10). You can use this Breath Weapon a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest

effects.name: Draconic Flight
effects.notes: When you reach character level 5, you can channel draconic magic to give yourself temporary flight. As a Bonus Action, you sprout spectral wings on your back that last for 10 minutes or until you retract the wings (no action required) or have the Incapacitated condition. During that time, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed. Your wings appear to be made of the same energy as your Breath Weapon. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

feats.notes: Battle Medic. If you have a Healer's Kit, you can expend one use of it and tend to a creature within 5 feet of yourself as a Utilize action. That creature can expend one of its Hit Point Dice, and you then roll that die. The creature regains a number of Hit Points equal to the roll plus your Proficiency Bonus.Healing Rerolls. Whenever you roll a die to determine the number of Hit Points you restore with a spell or with this feat's Battle Medic benefit, you can reroll the die if it rolls a 1, and you must use the new roll.
feats.name: Healer

feats.notes: Potent Poison. When you make a damage roll that deals Poison damage, it ignores Resistance to Poison damage.Brew Poison. You gain proficiency with the Poisoner's Kit. With 1 hour of work using such a kit and expending 50 GP worth of materials, you can create a number of poison doses equal to your Proficiency Bonus. As a Bonus Action, you can apply a poison dose to a weapon or piece of ammunition. Once applied, the poison retains its potency for 1 minute or until you deal damage with the poisoned item, whichever is shorter. When a creature takes damage from the poisoned item, that creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the modifier of the ability increased by this feat and your Proficiency Bonus) or take 2d8 Poison damage and have the Poisoned condition until the end of your next turn.
feats.name: Poisoner
